title: Pets, dog walking and arthritis with frailty (UK)

meta_description: Keeping a pet with arthritis and frailty: safer dog walking, avoiding falls from leads and trips, help with care, and planning ahead for your pet.
excerpt: Keeping a pet with arthritis and frailty: safer dog walking, avoiding falls from leads and trips, help with care, and planning ahead for your pet.
direct_answer: Pets give company and a reason to move, but dogs pulling on leads and pets underfoot can cause falls. Training, the right lead, help with walks and planning ahead can make pet ownership safer.
author: Louis Maxwell
keywords: pets, dog walking, falls, arthritis, frailty, companionship, UK
content:
Pets can be good for wellbeing.

This guide covers staying safe. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Dog walking

  • Use a lead that does not wrap around your hand.
  • Consider training for pulling.
  • Walk on even paths.

Indoors

Watch for pets underfoot; use a night light.

Help with care

Charities and neighbours may help with walks.

Planning ahead

Arrange who would care for your pet if you are unwell.

When to get help

  • Call 999 or go to A&E if someone suddenly becomes confused. Many causes need immediate assessment. Do not assume it is a urine infection, dementia or a medicine effect. Do not drive yourself to A&E; ask someone else to drive or call 999. Stay with the person and reassure them while help is arranged.
  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for a sudden drop in mobility or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Is a dog good exercise?

It can be.

What if I cannot walk them?

Ask for help.

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
